brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Decay Calculator" that helps elderly users with dementia track which memories are fading fastest by representing each memory as a physical object dissolving in acid a

dominant_strengths: The dissolving-beaker metaphor is conceptually strong and ties physical decay to memory loss in an evocative literal way.
Clean sans-serif headers and label uppercase tracking show typographic discipline in the title and form panel.
dominant_weaknesses: Catastrophic layout failure: three floating beakers with no labels, no axes context, and a header card detached top-left.
Severely fails the elderly/dementia audience—tiny labels, low-contrast greens, abstract icons, no memory names visible, cognitive load is high.
Color palette is uniformly green across all three samples, defeating the 'fading fastest' comparison the brief demands.
fix_priorities: Label each beaker with the memory description, type, and a clear decay percentage so users can actually compare fade rates.
Map fill color to decay state (vivid→pale→ghost) so the fastest-fading memory is instantly visceral.
Redesign for accessibility: larger type, higher contrast, simplified controls, and a calm reassuring tone for dementia users.
Anchor the floating panels into a coherent grid with shared baselines and a legend.
rationale.norman_balance: Weak on all three levels—visceral metaphor exists but is muted, behavioral usability is broken by missing labels, and reflective meaning never lands.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially captures the dissolving-object metaphor but fails the actual brief because elderly users cannot read, compare, or emotionally engage with the unlabeled beakers.
